# How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Mass

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. Their changing separation is the measurement at the center of the mission: as gravity acts on the pair, the distance between them shifts.

As the satellites approach a larger concentration of mass, stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite. Scientists use these changes in distance as raw measurements to infer shifts in mass on Earth. Those estimates help them investigate changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
